mainTopic: Acts of חזקה that acquire property: neighboring fields and houses, ownerless land of a גר, and acquiring a slave through service or lifting
overview: This amud is about acquiring property through חזקה, an act of ownership. First it finishes a ruling about two fields with a מצר (boundary strip) between them. A חזקה on one field acquires only that field, and only if he meant to acquire it. רבי זירא and רבי אלעזר then ask whether the מצר can link the two fields, and both questions end in תיקו. רב נחמן gives similar rules for two houses, one behind the other. There is one difference: a חזקה on the inner house can acquire both houses, because the inner house's way in and out runs through the outer one. Next come rulings about the land of a גר who died without heirs. Hanging doors on palaces someone else built acquires them, and so does a coat of plaster or tile an אמה in size opposite the doorway, or spreading out mattresses. רב ששת supports the mattress ruling with a ברייתא about acquiring a slave through his service. The גמרא then explains that רבי שמעון holds a master can also acquire a slave by lifting him. The amud ends as a new teaching of רב יהודה begins.

steps.title: Acquiring one field does not acquire the field next to it
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the earlier ruling about two fields with a מצר between them. A חזקה on one field meant to cover both acquires only the first field. A חזקה meant only for the other field acquires nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did a חזקה on one field intending to acquire it and also the other field, he acquires the first field but not the other. If he intended to acquire only the other field, he does not acquire even the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ruling about two fields separated by a boundary. It explains what happens when the buyer's intention reaches past the field he actually worked on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה works only on the field where the act was done, so the other field is not acquired. When his intention was only for the other field, the act also fails on the first field, because he never meant to acquire it.

keyTerms.meaning: to acquire, to take legal ownership
its companion, meaning the other field

steps.confusionAlert: In the last case he actually did the work on the first field, yet he still does not acquire it. Acquiring needs the intention to acquire that specific property.

phrases.english: [If he took possession of one field] to acquire it and the other one,
he acquired it, but did not acquire the other one.
[If he took possession of it] to acquire only the other one,
he did not acquire even this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ruling that began before this section, about two fields with one boundary between them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזקה acquires only the field it was done on, and only if he intended to acquire that field. It never reaches the neighboring field.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the baseline that the next two questions build on: the fields count as separate, and intention decides what is acquired.

steps.title: Does including the boundary connect the two fields?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks about someone who does a חזקה on one field intending to acquire it, the מצר, and the other field. Does the shared מצר join the fields into one unit, or does each field stay separate?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: if someone took possession of one field to acquire it, the boundary, and the other field, what is the law? Do we say the boundary makes the land one unit, so he acquires everything? Or does each field stand on its own?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks a new question that builds on the ruling just stated. He gives two possible ways to look at it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 1 he intended both fields but left out the מצר, and he acquired only the first field. Here he also intends to acquire the מצר. The question is whether the מצר, as a shared piece of land, ties the two fields together into one property.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked a question that has no clear answer yet
took possession by doing an act of ownership (חֲזָקָה)
stands by itself, counts as separate

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked:
If he took possession of one of them
in order to acquire it, and the boundary,
and the other one, what is the law?
Do we say: the boundary of the land
is one, so he acquires [everything];
phrases.notes: He means the shared boundary joins both fields into one piece of land.

phrases.english: or perhaps this one stands by itself
and that one stands by itself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the boundary to the buyer's intention and asks whether that changes the result of step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether intending to acquire the shared מצר links the two fields, so that a חזקה on one field acquires both.

steps.title: רבי זירא's question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The question stays open with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand: the question is not answered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רבי זירא's question without deciding it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether the מצר joins the fields. The doubt remains.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand, meaning the question stays unanswered

phrases.english: Let it stand [unresolved].

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It is unresolved whether including the מצר in one's intention lets a חזקה on one field acquire the other field.

steps.title: Can taking the boundary acquire both fields, like a halter?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks about someone who does a חזקה on the מצר itself, intending to acquire both fields. Is the מצר like a halter (אפסרא) that pulls the whole animal with it, or is each field separate?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked: if someone took possession of the boundary in order to acquire both fields, what is the law? Do we say the boundary is like the land's halter, so he acquires the fields? Or does each field stand on its own?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר asks a different question. This time the act of ownership is done on the boundary strip itself, not on either field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can acquire an animal by taking hold of its halter, because the halter is attached to the animal. The question is whether the מצר is attached to the fields in the same way, so that taking the מצר brings both fields along.

keyTerms.meaning: a halter, the rope used to lead an animal

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked:
If he took possession of the boundary to acquire both of them, what is the law?
Do we say that this boundary
is the halter of the land, so he acquires [them];
phrases.notes: Picture leading a whole animal by its rope: maybe the boundary pulls the fields along the same way.

phrases.english: or perhaps this one stands by itself
and that one stands by itself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel question: the act of ownership is now done on the מצר instead of on one of the fields.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a חזקה on the מצר works like taking an animal's halter and acquires both fields attached to it.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's question is also left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: This question also ends in תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand: the question is not answered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רבי אלעזר's question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It stays undecided whether the מצר counts as the fields' halter. So it is unclear whether a חזקה on the מצר acquires both fields.
steps.whatToRemember: Two fields with a מצר between them are treated as separate properties. A חזקה on one field acquires only that field, and only with the right intention. Whether the מצר can link the two fields is an open question, both in רבי זירא's case and in רבי אלעזר's case.

phrases.english: Let it stand [unresolved].

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It is unresolved whether a חזקה on the מצר acquires both fields.

steps.title: The same rules apply to two houses, one behind the other
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, in the name of רבה בר אבוה, rules about two houses where one is behind the other. A חזקה on the outer house acquires it. Intending to acquire both acquires only the outer house. Intending to acquire only the inner house acquires nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: there are two houses, one inside the other. If he took possession of the outer house to acquire it, he acquires it. If he meant to acquire it and the inner house, he acquires the outer house but not the inner one. If he meant to acquire only the inner house, he does not acquire even the outer one.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives a ruling about houses that matches the three rules for fields in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the inner house is acquired along with the outer one, since you reach it through the outer house. The ruling says no: each house is separate, just like the fields. Intention still decides: if he meant only the inner house, the act on the outer house acquires nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: further inside than the other one

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule from the fields also applies to houses when the חזקה is done on the outer house. Even though the inner house can only be reached through the outer one, a חזקה on the outer house does not reach the inner house. The next step shows that the opposite direction works differently.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
[If there are] two houses, this one further inside than that one,
and he took possession of the outer one to acquire it, he acquired it.
[If he did it] to acquire it and the inner one,
he acquired the outer one, but did not acquire the inner one.
[If he did it] to acquire only the inner one,
he did not acquire even the outer one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the pattern of step 1 and applies the same three rules to houses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזקה on the outer house acquires only the outer house, and only if he intended to acquire it. It never acquires the inner house.

steps.title: A חזקה on the inner house
steps.stepSummary: This continues רב נחמן's ruling. A חזקה on the inner house acquires it. Intending to acquire both houses acquires both. Intending to acquire only the outer house acquires nothing, not even the inner one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did a חזקה on the inner house to acquire it, he acquired it. If he meant to acquire it and the outer house, he acquired both. If he meant to acquire only the outer house, he did not even acquire the inner one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב נחמן's ruling about two houses, one behind the other. It now covers the case where the חזקה was done on the inner house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of the outer-house case from step 6. From the inner house you can reach both houses, since the inner house uses the outer one as its way in and out, so intending both works. But if he only wanted the outer house, his action on the inner house was not aimed at anything he was actually holding, so he gets nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner house (the one further in)
The outer house (the one closer to the street)
He did a חזקה, an act of taking possession

steps.whatToRemember: Outer house: a חזקה there acquires only the outer house. Inner house: a חזקה there can acquire both houses if he intends both. Aiming at a house you did not touch gets you nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 6. There, intending both houses got only the outer one. Here, intending both gets both, because the inner house's way in and out runs through the outer house, so the outer house is tied to the inner one.

phrases.english: If he did a חזקה on the inner one to acquire it, he acquired it.
If he did it to acquire it and the outer one,
he acquired both of them.
If he did it to acquire the outer one,
he did not acquire even the inner one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב נחמן's two-house ruling by giving the inner-house case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזקה on the inner house acquires it, acquires both houses if he intends both, and acquires nothing if he intends only the outer house.

steps.title: Hanging doors on palaces someone else built
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, in the name of רבה בר אבוה, rules: if one person builds large palaces on the property of a גר who died without heirs, and another person puts doors on them, the one who put on the doors acquires them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone builds large palaces on a dead גר's property, and another person comes and sets up doors for them, the second person acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling about ownerless property: the person who finishes the building by hanging doors wins it, not the person who built it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising, since the builder did much more work. The ruling teaches that what counts is the act that makes the property usable and complete, not the amount of labor. The reason comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The property of a גר who died without heirs, which becomes ownerless

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה:
One who builds large palaces
on the property of a גר,
phrases.notes: He means a גר who died with no heirs, so his land has no owner and anyone can take it.

phrases.english: and another came and set up doors for them,
acquired it.
phrases.notes: It is the second person, the one who hung the doors, who acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: הַבּוֹנֶה פַּלְטֵרִין גְּדוֹלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the two-house case to a new case about building on ownerless land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The person who puts doors on palaces built on a dead גר's land acquires them, not the builder.

steps.title: Why the builder doesn't acquire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the door-hanger acquires and answers that the first person only moved bricks around. An unfinished building is not a real act of possession.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The first one only turned over bricks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind step 8 and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building walls without doors leaves something that is not yet a usable house, so legally it is just piling up bricks. Hanging the doors turns it into a real, usable house, and that is the act that counts as a חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: That he turned over, moved around

phrases.english: What is the reason?
The first one merely turned over bricks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for the ruling in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the door-hanger acquire and not the builder?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The builder only moved bricks around. Without doors the building is not complete, so his work is not a חזקה.

steps.title: One coat of plaster or one tile acquires
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי בר יוסף, in the name of רבי אלעזר, rules: someone who finds palaces on a dead גר's property and puts one coat of plaster or one tile on them acquires them.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who finds palaces on a גר's property and plasters them with one coat of plaster or one tile acquires them.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ruling about ownerless buildings: even a small improvement, like a bit of plaster or tiling, is enough of a חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike step 8, here the building already exists and the finder adds an improvement. Even a small decorative upgrade shows ownership and counts as a חזקה. How big it has to be is asked in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Plastering, a coat of plaster or whitewash
Tiling or decorative work on a wall or floor

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב דִּימִי בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: רב דימי בר יוסף said in the name of רבי אלעזר:
One who finds palaces on the property of a גר,
and plasters them with one coat of plaster
or one tile,
acquired them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב דִּימִי בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another type of act that counts as a חזקה on a dead גר's buildings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single coat of plaster or one tile on found palaces acquires them.

steps.title: How much plaster is needed: one אמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how big the plastered or tiled area must be. רב יוסף answers: an אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much? רב יוסף said: a cubit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the minimum size of the plastering in step 10, and רב יוסף gives it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "One coat" was vague, so the גמרא sets a minimum. A square אמה is enough to be a real improvement and not just a smudge.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, about the length of a forearm

phrases.english: And how much?
רב יוסף said: a cubit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the size needed for the plaster or tile ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the minimum area of plaster or tile needed to acquire?

steps.title: The plaster must face the entrance
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא adds a condition: the plaster or tile must be opposite the entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: and it must be opposite the doorway.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a second condition to the plaster ruling: where the work is placed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "and" shows he is adding to רב יוסף's size rule, not arguing with it. So the work must be an אמה and also placed opposite the doorway.
steps.whatToRemember: To acquire found buildings with plaster or tile, the work must be an אמה in size (רב יוסף) and opposite the entrance (רב חסדא).

phrases.english: רב חסדא said: and opposite the doorway.
phrases.notes: The word "and" means he is adding to רב יוסף: an אמה, and also placed opposite the doorway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a location requirement on top of רב יוסף's size requirement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The plaster or tile acquires only if it is opposite the entrance.

steps.title: Spreading mattresses acquires
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם reports that רב ששת taught: someone who spreads out mattresses on a dead גר's property acquires it. רב עמרם adds that רב ששת showed them a proof from a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said: רב ששת told us this, and he lit up our eyes from a ברייתא: one who spreads out mattresses on a גר's property acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling: using the property in a normal way, like spreading out bedding, counts as a חזקה. רב עמרם also mentions that רב ששת had a proof, which the next step brings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the act is not building or improving at all. It is just using the place the way an owner would. The mention of a proof from a ברייתא sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One who spreads out mattresses or bedding
He lit up our eyes, he showed us clearly
A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה

phrases.english: רב עמרם said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מִילְּתָא אֲמַר לַן רַב שֵׁשֶׁת,
phrases.english: This matter רב ששת told us,
and he lit up our eyes from a ברייתא:
phrases.notes: In other words, רב ששת showed them a ברייתא that backs this up. The next step tells us which one.

phrases.english: one who spreads out mattresses on the property of a גר
acquired it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם: הַאי מִילְּתָא אֲמַר לַן רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another kind of act that counts as a חזקה on a dead גר's property, this time simple use instead of building.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spreading mattresses on a dead גר's property acquires it.

steps.title: The ברייתא about acquiring a slave through service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which ברייתא רב ששת meant and quotes it: a slave is acquired through חזקה when he serves his new master, by putting on or taking off his shoes, carrying his things to the bathhouse, undressing, bathing, anointing, scraping, dressing, putting on his shoes, or lifting him.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the ברייתא that lit up our eyes? It was taught: how is a slave acquired by חזקה? If he put on his shoe, untied his shoe, carried his things after him to the bathhouse, undressed him, bathed him, anointed him, scraped him, dressed him, put on his shoes, or lifted him, he acquired him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which ברייתא רב ששת was referring to and brings it as the source for his mattress ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, everyday acts of use, a slave serving his master, count as a חזקה. That supports רב ששת: using property in a normal way, like spreading bedding, is also a חזקה. The גמרא quotes the ברייתא without spelling out the connection.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
How does one acquire through חזקה?

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is about acquiring a slave, not land. The connection is that in both cases ordinary use counts as a חזקה.

phrases.english: "And he lit up our eyes from a ברייתא" — what is it?
As it was taught: how is it done through חזקה?
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is talking about acquiring a slave. It doesn't say so here, but it is assumed.

phrases.english: If he put on his shoe for him,
phrases.notes: The slave is the one doing these services for the new master.

phrases.english: or untied his shoe for him,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהוֹלִיךְ כֵּלָיו אַחֲרָיו לְבֵית הַמֶּרְחָץ,
phrases.english: or carried his things after him to the bathhouse,
or undressed him, or bathed him,
anointed him, scraped him,
phrases.notes: Scraping means rubbing the oil and dirt off his skin after the bath.

phrases.english: or dressed him, or put on his shoes,
or lifted him, he acquired him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַנְהֲרִינְהוּ עַיְנִין מִמַּתְנִיתָא – מַאי הִיא? דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies and quotes the ברייתא that רב ששת used to support his mattress ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's ruling that spreading mattresses on a dead גר's property acquires it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing personal services by a slave that count as a חזקה for acquiring him.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: lifting acquires everywhere
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, רבי שמעון comments that a חזקה should not be stronger than lifting, because lifting acquires in every situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: a חזקה should not be greater than lifting, since lifting acquires everywhere.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון adds his own comment at the end of the ברייתא by comparing חזקה to lifting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His point is that lifting is the strongest kind of acquisition, since it works in every situation. So a חזקה should not have more power than lifting has. At first it is not clear what he is disputing, since the first תנא also listed lifting. Steps 16 and 17 explain this.

keyTerms.meaning: In every place, in every situation

steps.whatToRemember: The two ways to acquire in this ברייתא are חזקה (acts of use or service) and הגבהה (lifting). רבי שמעון holds that lifting is the stronger one, since it works everywhere.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון said:
A חזקה should not be greater than lifting,
since lifting acquires in every situation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: לֹא תְּהֵא חֲזָקָה גְּדוֹלָה מֵהַגְבָּהָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with רבי שמעון's comment comparing חזקה to lifting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזקה cannot be stronger than lifting, because lifting acquires in every situation.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון adding?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון's comment adds, since the ברייתא already listed lifting as a way to acquire a slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון means by his comment. It is setting up the explanation that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first תנא already listed 'lifting him' as a way to acquire a slave. So when רבי שמעון says lifting acquires everywhere, it sounds like he is repeating what was already said. The גמרא wants to know what the real disagreement is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? The גמרא asks for the meaning or point of a statement.

phrases.english: What is he saying?
phrases.notes: The puzzle is that the first תנא already said lifting works, so what is רבי שמעון adding?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the point of רבי שמעון's comment in Step 15, given the list in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What point רבי שמעון is making, since the first תנא also lists lifting as a way to acquire.

steps.title: Slave lifting master vs. master lifting slave
steps.stepSummary: The first תנא holds that only the slave lifting his master acquires him. רבי שמעון holds that the master lifting the slave also acquires, because lifting acquires everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is saying: If the slave lifted his master, the master acquires him. If the master lifted the slave, he does not acquire him. רבי שמעון said: חזקה should not be stronger than הגבהה, because הגבהה acquires in every situation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first תנא's 'lifting him' as the slave lifting the master. It then shows that רבי שמעון disagrees about the master lifting the slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first תנא, lifting counts only as service. The slave works for the master by lifting him, which is a חזקה. When the master lifts the slave, the slave has done no service, so the master does not acquire him. רבי שמעון says plain lifting is a full קנין everywhere, so the master acquires the slave by lifting him.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is saying. It introduces the explanation of a statement.

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree a slave who lifts his master is acquired by service (חזקה). They argue only about a master who lifts the slave. The first תנא says this does not acquire, and רבי שמעון says it does, because הגבהה works everywhere.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of lifting. The slave lifting the master is service (חזקה). The master lifting the slave is a physical הגבהה of the slave himself. They are two different ways of acquiring.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
If he lifted his master, the master acquires him;
if his master lifted him, he does not acquire him.
Rabbi Shimon said:
Taking possession should not be greater than lifting,
for lifting acquires in every situation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by reading the ברייתא so that a real disagreement appears.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first תנא counts only the slave lifting his master. רבי שמעון adds that the master lifting the slave also acquires, since הגבהה acquires everywhere.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that חזקה through service and הגבהה are separate kinds of קנין. רבי שמעון holds that הגבהה is always at least as strong as חזקה.

steps.title: New teaching of רב ירמיה ביראה begins
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה ביראה begins quoting a new ruling of רב יהודה. Only the first words appear here.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה ביראה said in the name of רב יהודה: This one who...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new statement from רב יהודה, passed on by רב ירמיה ביראה. Only the opening words are here, and the ruling itself continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'הַאי מַאן' (this one who) open a case about a certain kind of person. The actual case and ruling come next, so for now we only know who is speaking.

keyTerms.meaning: רב ירמיה of בירא, the אמורא who reports this teaching.
This one who... An Aramaic opening for a case about someone who does something.

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya Bira'a says
that Rav Yehuda says:
With regard to this one who

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the slave discussion and opens a new teaching.
